chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Christian woman whose husband died while she was with him, and he was a Christian, what is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The waiting period of the free Muslim woman, four months and ten (days).'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a non-Muslim woman whose husband dies?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a free Christian woman whose husband dies while still a Christian observes the standard Muslim waiting period of four months and ten days. This ruling highlights the principle that the *iddah* is tied to the woman's status and the marital bond rather than the husband's religion at the time of death, distinguishing it from cases where the husband was Muslim. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for determining the rights and rituals of *Ahl al-Kitab* women within the Islamic legal framework.
